guardianfootball.title: Isak pounces to give Liverpool victory on Iraola’s return to Bournemouth
guardianfootball.description: At the final whistle, victory secured, Andoni Iraola embraced both his current players and those he guided to new heights at Bournemouth last season. Liverpool are not yet the overwhelming, suffocating force Iraola wants them to become but they did enough to claim three points here, Alexander Isak capping a peculiar performance with a simple finish. Cody Gakpo was again the architect, the Dutchman the supplier for all four of Isak’s goals this season. Isak’s only other shot before scoring was to balloon a first-time effort high and wide but his second-half strike was sufficient to return Liverpool to winning ways in the Premier League. Continue reading...

guardianfootball.title: ‘Mixed emotions’ for Farke as Leeds stay unbeaten with Crystal Palace stalemate
guardianfootball.description: Perhaps it is testament to the progress Leeds have made since returning to the Premier League just over a year ago that there was frustration at failing to move up to third after drawing with Crystal Palace. Instead, Daniel Farke’s team enter the prolonged international break in fifth and unbeaten, which is a fine achievement in itself. Apart from Tyrick Mitchell’s disallowed goal, neither side gave much impression they would secure the points. For Palace, it was a first clean sheet of the season, having conceded at least twice in their opening four games, relieving pressure on Pierre Sage, while the hosts endured their first blank. Continue reading...

guardianfootball.title: Rangers and Ryan Naderi finish off Celtic’s horror week with Old Firm victory
guardianfootball.description: If ever a stadium can be rocked by silence, this was the moment. With no visiting fans allowed at any of this season’s Glasgow derbies, Ryan Naderi’s winning goal was met with nothing but the banging of fists of the clear plastic of the Rangers bench, and the shouting of the broadcast commentators. A screaming void of apathy and atrophy, the sound of a beckoning abyss, of a title race blowing open and a team slowly breaking apart. That Rangers were unable to celebrate this triumph with their fans in the stadium was, of course, a source of lament, as well as a measure of just how ugly this fixture has become over the years. Continue reading...

guardianfootball.title: Zidane’s next move as France coach may reveal the wizard behind the curtain | Jonathan Wilson
guardianfootball.description: It is apt that the most perplexing football country will now be guided by the most enigmatic of leaders Even in his playing days, Zinedine Zidane seemed unknowable. As a manager, the sense of distance has only grown. He won three Champions Leagues with Real Madrid without ever giving a sense of what his idea of football looked like. France are perhaps the most perplexing football country: a squad that teems with such talent that a B team would be serious contenders at a World Cup, that reached three major finals under Didier Deschamps with a sense of unfulfilment, a team that progressed but rarely entranced, or at least didn’t until this summer’s World Cup, when they attacked with gusto…

guardianfootball.title: ‘We miss her the same every day’: Olivia Cusack on her late footballer sister Maddy
guardianfootball.description: Family is determined to ensure her ‘legacy lives on’ three years after the Sheffield United player’s death Olivia Cusack says her sister, the late Maddy Cusack, is on her mind every single day and she is determined to ensure her “legacy lives on” three years after the former England youth international midfielder’s death. Olivia, together with family and friends of Maddy, walked 29 miles from Bramall Lane, Sheffield United’s home, to their family’s home in Horsley, near Derby, on Saturday to raise funds and awareness. Maddy’s loved ones are still enduring a “frustrating and confusing” wait for answers about the circumstances surrounding her death on 20 September 2023. Continue reading...

pitchfork.title: Easy Rider (Music From the Soundtrack)
pitchfork.description: Each Sunday, Pitchfork takes an in-depth look at a significant album from the past, and any record not in our archives is eligible. Today, we revisit the blockbuster soundtrack for the 1969 biker classic: a generational bounty of radio hits that, taken together, sounds like a dying dream.

pitchfork.title: Second Song
pitchfork.description: The 80-year-old musician’s 50th studio album emphasizes atmosphere over songcraft, but its long, rambling tracks offer ample reminders of his melodic dexterity and lyrical gifts.

pitchfork.title: Day and Night
pitchfork.description: Carly Rae Jepsen’s sprawling new double album celebrates full-time love and commitment with sweet, sunny tracks for Day and sleeker, dancier songs for Night.

pitchfork.title: Pylon
pitchfork.description: Members of Turnstile, Deftones, Paramore, and Pinegrove push Bea Kristi toward slightly grungier, angstier territory on her fourth album.

pitchfork.title: Angel
pitchfork.description: After going viral with swooning, rom-com-ready songs, the singer-songwriter takes a more homespun approach on her fourth album, a set of folk-influenced tracks buoyed by a wandering spirit.

pitchfork.title: Secret to Spare
pitchfork.description: On its debut album, the refreshingly sincere L.A. power-pop quartet wears its heart—and its influences—on its sleeve.

pitchfork.title: lucy miró al mundo y notó que está girando
pitchfork.description: With an assist from Jane Remover and under the influence of the Beatles, the rising Chilean star crafts a digirock ode to emotional overload.

pitchfork.title: Wet
pitchfork.description: Steamy and subversive, the new album from former LCD Soundsystem collaborator Gavilán Rayna Russom’s long-running project is a queer electro manifesto.

quietus.title: Food For Thought: Lupe Fiasco’s Food & Liquor at 20
quietus.description: Lupe Fiasco's fabulous first LP was a debut for the ages.... but how come they don't make 'em like this any more? Angus Batey asks As loyal subscribers will know – and if you're not one already, what's keeping you? Click that button up there at the top of the page immediately! – September 2026 has seen Luke and John celebrating this august organ's coming of age. Such occasions are always potent – useful staging posts and rest stops before the never-ending journey forward continues; opportunities to reflect and reminisce – and so it is with these anniversary pieces. Especially for this ageing hack, who is always forcibly reminded of his own ongoing meander into disconnected irrelevance when…

quietus.title: Enough of the Self and its Dilemmas! An Interview with Missouri Williams
quietus.description: The English novelist, author of Doloriad and The Vivisectors talks campus novels, Coil's 'Fire of the Mind' and her surprise longlisting for this year's Booker Prize In a never-repeated episode of the BBC arts documentary series Omnibus broadcast on 27 September 1991 titled ‘The Word, The Image, And The Gun’, American writer Don Delillo spoke of his obsession with the television screen. Throughout the documentary, we cut to Delillo; who sits within an empty cinema watching images of the Kennedy assassination on a loop or at his typewriter over-looking Manhattan traffic, with footage of the Lockerbie Bomber or the Iranian Hostage Crisis opaquely overlaid. And from within this gust of sharp,…

quietus.title: Inner Ear: Macedonian Music for September by Jakub Knera
quietus.description: In North Macedonia the leftfield scene has thrived for decades in spite of a major lack of musical infrastructure. In his latest guide to the underground music of Central and Eastern Europe, Jakub Knera explores why Sepak Se Vrti' Festival, Gostivar “We have this inside joke: how many people from Stotrojka does it take to change a light bulb? How does it all work, and how on earth has that radio station survived for 35 years? I’ve no idea. It must be some glitch in the system,” says Gjorgji Janevski, one of those without whom it would be difficult to tell the story of Macedonian independent music. This “glitch in the system” is a fitting metaphor for a scene that has thrived...

quietus.title: Compilation of the Week: Plata’s Safn
quietus.description: Archie Forde hails a compilation of young Icelandic electronic music makers, austere experimentalists and noisemongers, which rails against gentrification and foreclosed futures alike safn by plata It’s October 2025, and Icelandic noise music collective Spider Network are crammed into a Reykjavik beer garden, working late into the night. Spools of vermillion thread cling to the space’s tarp roof; one member laboriously unwraps tinfoil and plasters it across plastic windows and walls; a ritual doll is suspended from the ceiling. This haunting decor is being assembled for Falconfest, a noise show held in Reykjavik venue Lemmy in collaboration with No Borders, a charity dedicated to providing…

quietus.title: Actress – Radical Frame
quietus.description: Actress Radical Frame Making his return to the Ninja Tune label, Darren Cunningham practices typical elusiveness with doleful piano stabs amidst pounding surf and ambient textures Radical Frame by Actress Try to recall an Actress track and you won’t bring a melody or rhythm back. You’ll find only a noir sensation, the faint memory of wading through a city’s hazy silence at four in the morning, alone, but with something in the air around you that the skin registers before the mind does. A rusting Weltschmerz bleeds through Darren Cunningham’s music, dissolving evanescent motifs into lasting affect. Over twenty years into his career, Radical Frame sees the UK producer continue to explore…

quietus.title: Spiritual Goth: Nigel Godrich’s Favourite Albums
quietus.description: Ahead of a new album with Dhani Harrison, superproducer Nigel Godrich tells Elizabeth Aubrey about the 13 records that have soundtracked his life and career, from the "unparalleled" Joni Mitchell to the "high art" of Grace Jones Photo by Darian Zahedi “This was completely impossible,” Nigel Godrich laughs from LA, where he is busy in rehearsals. He is referring here not to his prep for upcoming live shows – to be performed with musician Dhani Harrison for their exciting new musical project, Dragonflies – but to the task of narrowing his favourite album choices down to just 13. “I’ve ended up choosing records that are not necessarily my favourite album by that artist, but they represent…

quietus.title: Organic Intelligence LX: Nigerian Alté
quietus.description: In this month’s antidote to the algorithm, Mary Chiney introduces tQ subscribers to a subculture that thrived on the fringes of the Afrobeats explosion Lady Donli, via artist's Bandcamp If you cast an eye toward West Africa over the last decade, you’d be forgiven for viewing Nigerian music as a cultural giant. The global explosion of Afrobeats, a very polished juggernaut led for many years by the likes of Burna Boy, Wizkid, and Davido, has dominated the narrative, filling dancefloors from London to Los Angeles. At the same time, beneath mainstream Lagos, a quiet rebellion has emerged. It happened on SoundCloud, at underground thrift pop-ups, and in the bedrooms of kids who felt entirely…

quietus.title: Not the How But the What: Lummernikt by Finn Loxbo
quietus.description: For all its stunning virtuosity, the tumbling fingerstyle guitar of Swedish guitarist Finn Loxbo is always in service to a set of brilliant compositional ideas Digging through the various improvised solo and duo recordings Swedish guitarist Finn Loxbo has made over the last decade is like witnessing a slow-motion creative winnowing, observing how a feverish pile of ideas and experiments has gradually coalesced into something inscrutable. His third solo album Lummernikt is a work of astonishing focus and originality forged from familiar notions, a free improvisation practice patiently chiseled into compositional rigour. Across eight riveting acoustic pieces played live without overdubs,…

aquariumdrunkard.title: Radio Free Aquarium Drunkard :: September 2026
aquariumdrunkard.description: Freeform transmissions from Radio Free Aquarium Drunkard on dublab. Airing every third Sunday of the month, RFAD on dublab features the pairing of Tyler Wilcox’s Doom and Gloom from the Tomb and Chad DePasquale’s New Happy Gathering. This month, Chad kicks it off with a roundup of recent 2026 digs. Tyler follows with an hour of existential daydreams and autumnal instrumentals. Sunday, 4-6pm PT.

aquariumdrunkard.title: Bandcamping :: Autumn 2026
aquariumdrunkard.description: Are things feeling autumnal at long last? Not quite. But maybe this selection of recommended sounds, old and new, can help usher in the cooler, crisper season. Bandcamp Friday only rolls around every couple of months. But remember, you can always add a buck or two to the asking price of any album on the platform and voila — every day is Bandcamp Friday.

aquariumdrunkard.title: Nigeria 80: The Explosive Sound World of 1980s Nigeria
aquariumdrunkard.description: The ’70s didn’t end. They just got more elastic. Strut’s Nigeria 80 catches Nigerian popular music in that beautiful, unruly stretch between Afrobeat’s explosion and whatever came next—juju, funk, highlife, reggae, proto-hip-hop, and plenty of glorious cross-pollination along the way.

aquariumdrunkard.title: The Lagniappe Sessions :: Instrumentals (2016-2026)
aquariumdrunkard.description: Aquarium Drunkard’s Lagniappe Sessions have been rolling along at a steady pace since 2011, bringing together a global lineup of artists to offer up cover versions of a few of their favorite tunes. And some of the most imaginative Lagniappes have been those that deliver purely instrumental pleasures, embracing melody, rhythm and texture. We’ve gathered together a 90-minute sampling of those covers from over the past decade, which range from MPB bliss-outs to Takoma School dreamscapes, from free-funk workouts to orchestral jazz. And beyond!

aquariumdrunkard.title: The Aquarium Drunkard Show: SIRIUS/XMU (7pm PDT, Channel 35)
aquariumdrunkard.description: Broadcasting from northeast Los Angeles — the Aquarium Drunkard Show on SIRIUS/XMU, channel 35. 7pm California time, Wednesdays. A signal from the afterlife of the ’60s—soft-focus surrealism, garage psych, baroque pop, pastoral folk, English eccentricity, studio alchemy and outsider visions. 34.1090° N, 118.2334° W

aquariumdrunkard.title: I Will Die In This Jean Jacket :: Hang From A Cloud
aquariumdrunkard.description: Minneapolis lifer Jim Blaha goes it alone on Hang From A Cloud, a raw, bedroom-recorded set of wistful garage-psych and punk songs that crackle with romantic desperation. From the breathy “Some New Day” to the furious, sotto voce anthems of “D.O.A.,” Blaha distills decades in the underground into something intimate, ferocious, and beautifully unvarnished.

aquariumdrunkard.title: Transmissions :: James Austin Johnson
aquariumdrunkard.description: This week on the show, comedian James Austin Johnson joins us to dive into the music nerd obsessions of his new comedy special ⁠He'll Yeah⁠. You've likely seen JAJ on the TV. He's known for portraying Donald Trump, Joe Biden, and occasionally, Bob Dylan, on SNL . But He’ll Yeah ’s vignettes and on-stage footage find Johnson creating a more "indie rock" styled special. Along the way, we talk Bob Dylan, the perils of political comedy, and much more.

aquariumdrunkard.title: Dollar Brand/Don Cherry/Carlos Ward :: The Third World-Underground
aquariumdrunkard.description: A live recording of three jazz masters in transitional phases of their careers, The Third World-Underground captures Abdullah Ibrahim (Dollar Brand), Don Cherry and Carlos Ward embarking on a joyous, lyrical and profoundly stomping set of tunes, teeming with fanfares, shouts and unruly dances. Newly reissued and remastered, this once Japanese-only release is ready to find its rightful audience. Where Ibrahim, Cherry and Ward are going, they don't need bass or drums.

mubi.title: The Action Scene | “The Raid” at 15
mubi.description: The Action Scene explores the form, history, and visceral power of action cinema through its set pieces. Clockwise from top-left: The Raid (Gareth Evans, 2011), Merantau (Gareth Evans, 2009), The Raid 2 (Gareth Evans, 2014), The Raid (Gareth Evans, 2011). It needs virtually no introduction. Fifteen years after its world premiere in the Midnight Madness section of the 2011 Toronto International Film Festival, The Raid (2011) has so shaped the landscape of contemporary action cinema that it’s birthed its own prepositional descriptor: “like The Raid ” adorns sundry headlines to describe any action film featuring some combination of a single-location setting, gritty atmosphere, barbarous…

mubi.title: Defending the Elusive
mubi.description: Last Year in Marienbad (Alain Resnais, 1961). 1 Although it’s seldom acknowledged, one of the supreme pleasures of movies is the confusion and uncertainty often prompted by the beginning of a story, when we’re not yet fully tuned in to what’s going on. As in our sleeping dreams, a sense of infinite possibility stretches before us. That seemingly limitless vista soon disappoints once it is foreshortened into something real and recognizable, such as a place, an environment, a mood, a character, a theme, a genre, or a plot. Yet without these comfortable anchors, something that resembles prenatal bliss envelops our ignorance, and the fact that we can imagine almost anything makes the start of…

mubi.title: Venice Dispatch: The Garden of Forking Paths
mubi.description: NAZA (Yuval Abraham and Rachel Szor, 2026). To watch my first film at the 83rd Venice Film Festival, I wore a VR headset. I say “watch” when the more accurate verb would be “experience,” at least going by the fest’s preferred vocabulary for what goes down on Lazzaretto Vecchio, an island a stone’s throw away from the Lido. Once used as a checkpoint for Holy Land pilgrims, and then—after the plague reached the lagoon in 1423—a leper colony, it is, in 2026 AD, now home to the virtual reality sidebar. The architecture has barely changed through the centuries. Dotting the high-ceilinged corridors that used to house the city’s moribund, festival guests can find various booths, each promising…

mubi.title: Survival Tactics: A Locarno Critics Academy Correspondence
mubi.description: Notebook, in partnership with the Locarno Critics Academy, presents a series of critical correspondences in which this year’s participants look back at the Swiss film festival. In this final installment, three critics explore how “tendenko,” a Japanese term that implies isolating to survive a tsunami, resonated across the program. “We live in a state of apocalyptic fetishism,” a radio announcer proclaims in Ann Oren’s Objet A (2026), and the slate of films at Locarno this August did little to dissuade its spectators of this assessment. As has been everywhere observed in recent years, the constant sounding of the alarm has become the 21st century’s room tone, and film festivals are not…

mubi.title: Cut and Spliced: A Locarno Critics Academy Correspondence
mubi.description: Notebook, in partnership with the Locarno Critics Academy, presents a series of critical correspondences in which this year’s participants look back at the Swiss film festival. In this second installment, four critics muse on cinema’s ability to splice disparate fragments together. They touch on ecstatic New York sirens, self-preservation in Iran and Palestine, performances that bear the weight of passing time, and an actress’s descent into two-faced delirium in Rome. We hear in Sans soleil (1983) that “Nothing sorts out memories from ordinary moments. It is only later that they claim remembrance, when they show their scars.” This is how I feel about memories all the time. What lingers in…

In a statement, Streep describes Loktev as “the Samuel Pepys of Putin’s Russia” and describes her films as a “blazing achievement.”…

mubi.title: It Was Once Fire: A Locarno Critics Academy Correspondence
mubi.description: Notebook, in partnership with the Locarno Critics Academy, presents a series of critical correspondences in which this year's participants look back at the Swiss film festival. In this first installment, letters exchanged between three critics contour what was on screen—broken relations, recalcitrant presences—with their experiences of Locarno beyond the frame. Photo by Alyssandra Maxine. Dear Vedant and Max, I’m writing you from the real world, which is to say, from my desk in my apartment in Brooklyn. The first few days of the festival seem very far away now, as they did even when I last saw you only five days ago. During a festival, time tends to go by like that: very quickly and also…

mubi.title: The Final Temenos
mubi.description: Photo by Emma Fuchs. At sunset we move like a herd. Arms laden with blankets, we snake down the gravel path, as signs in blue spray paint warn “ΠΡΟΣΟΧΗ! Use Caution!” Halfway there, the trees that bracket us part like curtains. Below, stark against the green-gold valley, we can make out a small white square—the projection screen. At a fork in the path, there is a small sign with a blue arrow on it, and the word “Temenos.” From here, the path narrows until suddenly it opens onto a clearing. In a small field, like a basin, rows of red beanbag chairs dot the ground in front of the screen, and behind them, a crescent of pink cushioned benches and a projector wait. The restoration of Eniaios…
